summary: Earnings analysis for Apple Inc. is constructive but execution-sensitive. The latest actual period shows a return to positive revenue momentum and resilient EPS, while the forecast assumes meaningful margin expansion through the outer years. For Apple, the earnings debate is less about near-term revenue growth alone and more about whether product refresh cycles, services monetization, pricing/mix discipline, and installed-base retention can sustain operating leverage. Given the valuation premium, investors should focus on gross margin guidance, Services growth, iPhone replacement demand, AI-related product adoption, China exposure, and regulatory pressure.
key_points: Apple Inc. generated $416.2B of revenue in 2025A; latest observed revenue growth was 6.4%, providing the starting point for the earnings forecast.
Year-over-year revenue growth was 6.4%, indicating a constructive recovery in top-line momentum.

EPS increased to $7.49 in 2025A and is forecast to reach $8.93 by 2027E; the implied earnings upside depends on sustaining revenue growth while converting margin expansion into per-share profit growth.
EBITDA is forecast to increase from $144.4B in 2025A to $215.8B in 2027E; this makes operating leverage and margin execution the central earnings debate.

EBITDA margin is projected to expand from 34.7% in 2025A to 44.8% in 2027E; the magnitude of this step-up should be treated as an important execution assumption rather than a mechanical extrapolation.
Contribution margin is expected to rise from 46.9% to 49.9%, supporting the earnings growth outlook through pricing discipline, services mix, and cost control.
SG&A margin is expected to move from 6.6% to 5.1%, indicating continued cost discipline.
watch_items: iPhone demand and premium-device replacement cycles
Gross margin and EBITDA margin guidance versus the implied forecast step-up
AI-related product adoption and competitive response
Regulatory pressure around App Store, payments, privacy, and platform control
